response.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT o.ordertune, COUNT(DISTINCT o.recordvault) AS n FROM orders o JOIN riskandmargin r ON r.ordervault = o.recordvault GROUP BY o.ordertune), a AS (SELECT AVG(n) AS av FROM c) SELECT AVG(c.n) AS avg_count_above_average, AVG(c.n - a.av) AS avg_excess_over_average FROM c CROSS JOIN a WHERE c.n > a.av

assumptions.assumption: Each order is counted once (distinct orders) even if it has several risk/margin records. Only orders with at least one match are counted.
The average across types is the plain average of the per-type counts. It includes only types that have at least one matched order. A NULL ordertune, if present, counts as its own group.

alternatives.interpretation: Count matched risk/margin records (join rows) per order type instead of distinct orders.
alternatives.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT o.ordertune, COUNT(*) AS n FROM orders o JOIN riskandmargin r ON r.ordervault = o.recordvault GROUP BY o.ordertune), a AS (SELECT AVG(n) AS av FROM c) SELECT AVG(c.n) AS avg_count_above_average, AVG(c.n - a.av) AS avg_excess_over_average FROM c CROSS JOIN a WHERE c.n > a.av
